brief.headline: They're losing money and carry heavy debt — secure a second source and offer faster payment for a ₹3.91 L/year price cut

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match the ₹290.00/KG we already pay Shrinath Roto Pack on our top laminates
priceAsk.basis: We pay ₹295.00/KG to GLS but only ₹290.00/KG to Shrinath for the same items — a 1.7% gap. The market asking price for pharma ORS laminate runs ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), so our current ₹295 sits at the top of fair. We should pay the best price we already get, not the highest.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (half our current 30) if they meet the ₹290/KG price
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹9.49 L of our cash, but they borrow money at about 10.96% — so 15 days early is worth roughly 0.45% of invoice value to them, a real win when they're bleeding cash

brief.financialLeverage: GLS made a loss in FY2024-25 (kept -3.4% vs 2.5% for similar firms) and owes 2.15x their own cash. Their money-health score is 2/10, they're in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.68), and they face severe legal cases, GST filing delays and EPF payment delays. Our ₹2.31 Cr is only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we're tiny to them — not a must-keep account. That means don't squeeze hard on price alone or we risk supply; instead lead with faster payment (which they badly need) and line up a backup. They already take 53d to pay their own suppliers (vs 36d peer median), so asking for better terms is only fair.

evidence.point: Their money-health score is very weak
They owe more than twice what they own
We pay ₹5/kg more than our cheapest supplier on the same laminates
They're in the distress grey zone
They borrow at a high rate and can barely cover interest

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter (already a tiny FDC supplier) — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant — both film substrate AND conversion; can second-source at scale

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter — pharma blister/sachet laminates; strong second-source (health D 31/100, revenue ₹222.04 Cr)

risks: They're losing money and in the grey distress zone — pushing too hard on price could tip them over and leave us scrambling for supply
We're only 0.33% of their revenue, so they won't bend over backwards to keep us — keep the tone collaborative
Credit rating is middling (IVR BBB- / Stable) and they face severe legal cases, GST delays and EPF delays — don't increase our exposure until we have a qualified second source lined up
If we cut them loose, lead-time to onboard Huhtamaki or UFLEX could be 8–12 weeks — start the second-source RFQ now, don't wait for this negotiation to fail
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but we're paying ₹295 here when our best laminate price is ₹290 — let's close that gap, and in return we can move you to 15-day payment to help your cash flow.
